The paired Δ 95% CI is [{{num:robustness.compare.qwen2.5-math-1.5b_vs_qwen2.5-1.5b.boot.delta_vs_qwen2.5-1.5b.ci.0:.3f}}, {{num:robustness.compare.qwen2.5-math-1.5b_vs_qwen2.5-1.5b.boot.delta_vs_qwen2.5-1.5b.ci.1:.3f}}]: no detectable effect.

**Abstraction axis (H-A4, Qwen3.5-2B).** After partialling out frequency and token count:
- PC1 correlates with LLM-judge abstraction at ρ = {{num:mvp.axes.qwen3.5-2b.pcs.0.rho_abstraction:.2f}} (twin {{num:mvp.axes.qwen3.5-2b__random.pcs.0.rho_abstraction:.2f}}).
- PC2 correlates with pure/applied at ρ = {{num:mvp.axes.qwen3.5-2b.pcs.1.rho_applied:.2f}}.
- The judges' ratings agree with an external, non-LLM measure, the import depth of each concept's definition in [Mathlib](https://github.com/leanprover-community/mathlib4): ρ = {{num:mvp.mathlib.rho_mean_rating_depth:.2f}}, 95% CI [{{num:mvp.mathlib.ci95.0:.2f}}, {{num:mvp.mathlib.ci95.1:.2f}}]. Only {{num:mvp.mathlib.n_matched}} of {{num:mvp.mathlib.n_math_concepts}} concepts could be matched, so this validation is weak.

**Methods check.** Partial RDM regression rejects a true null {{num:mvp.calibration.field_confounded_null.reject_rate_0.05:.0%}} of the time when the nuisance is a noisy proxy of a confounder. That is why the primary tests are paired twin contrasts.

### Figures

Each figure states what it shows, what to notice, and its main caveat. Pictures are unsupervised projections (PCA or MDS) of the same activations the statistics use, and every number is read from the results files. The pictures come from the preregistered confirmatory model, Qwen3.5-2B; the [interactive explorer](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/) shows all five models, every layer, and the twin.

#### Effect sizes for every confirmatory and added test

![forest plot]({{fig:forest}})

- **What you see:** each line is a 95% bootstrap CI, one per model or comparison. Blue means the CI excludes 0.
- **What to notice:**
  - The field map beats the random-init twin in all five models.
  - It beats fastText but not Qwen3-Embedding.
  - Math pretraining (H-A3) and the hierarchy test (H-A2) are nulls.
- **Caveat:** these CIs are unadjusted; the Holm decisions are in the scorecard. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-forest).

#### The map of mathematics

![field maps]({{fig:field_maps_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** 17 fields laid out by metric MDS for three distance matrices: arXiv cross-listing (ground truth), the trained model's field centroids, and the random-init twin's. Grey edges join each field to its 2 nearest arXiv neighbours, and they are drawn in every panel.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model most of these edges stay short, so algebraic fields sit together and the applied fields (orange) sit together. In the twin the edges cross the whole map.
  - Trained: ρ = {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.rsa.trained:.2f}}.
  - Twin: ρ = {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.rsa.random_init:.2f}}.
- **Caveat:**
  - ρ is computed on the full distance matrices, not on these 2-D pictures. Alignment (rotation and reflection) is for display only.
  - ρ ≈ {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.rsa.trained:.1f}} is a moderate correlation, and the picture shows that: several edges are long even in the trained model.
- [Interactive, with a layer slider](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-map).

![distance matrices]({{fig:field_rdms_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the same three distance matrices, colour = rank of each distance within its matrix (Spearman compares ranks). Rows are in one fixed order, grouped by the five super-tree branches.
- **What to notice:** the trained matrix partly reproduces the arXiv matrix's light algebra block and dark applied rows; the twin's matrix has no such structure.
- **Caveat:** a fixed row order is essential; re-clustering each matrix separately would create blocks out of noise. [Interactive, with linked hover](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-rdm).

![field map vs depth]({{fig:depth_curves}})

- **What you see:** ρ with arXiv at every layer, per model. The horizontal line is the 95th percentile of the max-over-layers permutation null. The vertical line marks the preregistered layer.
- **What to notice:**
  - The four Qwen models clear the null at every layer.
  - Gemma clears it at most depths but dips below it in two stretches.
  - Every twin stays at or below zero.
- **Caveat:** only the preregistered layer is a confirmatory test; any "best layer" is post-hoc. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-depth).

#### Shapes: circles for days and months, lines for chains, no circle for angles

![cyclic families]({{fig:cyclic_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the top-2 principal-component plane of each family; colour runs light → dark along the true order, and the grey path joins consecutive items.
- **What to notice:** days and months go round in their true order in the trained model (cycle score {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_plane_cycle.days.11.score:.2f}} and {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_plane_cycle.months.11.score:.2f}}), and not in the twin. For angles, the orange edge is the closure the preregistration predicted (330° next to 0°); in the model it spans the whole plot.
- **Caveat:**
  - Days and months are the positive control, and the PC-plane cycle score is post-hoc.
  - The cycle score also gives 1 to an open arc. In this plane the days' loop closes, but the months' Dec → Jan step is {{num:mvp.posthoc.qwen3.5-2b.pc_planes_cycle.months.11.planes.0.3:.1f}}× a neighbour step, so here they form an open arc. The closed-cycle test below checks this in every plane.
  - [Interactive, every family and layer](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-families).

The same planes through every layer, for the trained model and its twin, are animated [at the top of this README](#the-positive-control-layer-by-layer).

![angles: predicted vs found]({{fig:angles_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the preregistered prediction, what the model does, the bare numbers 0–330, and the random-init twin as a control.
- **What to notice:** the angles' geometry matches the numbers' (ρ = {{num:mvp.shapes.qwen3.5-2b.angles.beyond_reference.rho_fam_ref:.2f}}). The model encodes "330 degrees" by its numeral, not by its angle, which falsifies our prediction.
- **Caveat:**
  - Every random-init twin *meets* the preregistered circle rule (Qwen3.5-2B twin: closure {{num:mvp.shapes.qwen3.5-2b__random.angles.closure:.2f}}), because a structureless cloud passes it by chance. The informative result is the trained models' line-like order, not the failed rule.
  - This is one prompt format at this model scale. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-families).

#### Beyond the top-2 plane: the same families in 3-D

<p align="center"><img src="{{fig:turntable_qwen3.5-2b.gif}}" alt="Days, months and angles in their top-3 principal components, rotating; trained model top, random-init twin bottom" width="720"></p>

- **What you see:** days, months and angles in their top-3 principal components at the preregistered layer, rotating once. Trained model on top, random-init twin below. Each axis is that model's own PC and is labelled with its share of variance; proportions are true.
- **What to notice:** with a third axis the angles still run as an open path, 330° far from 0°. The days' loop is visible from every side.
- **Caveat:** a rotating picture is not a test. Numbers lie on helices with periodic parts beyond PC1–2 ([Kantamneni & Tegmark 2025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.00873)), so we tested every plane of the top-5 PCs for a loop that closes. The test is post-hoc, and was pre-specified in an [addendum](reports/prereg_addendum_3d.md) before it ran. Static version for every model: [`families3d_qwen3.5-2b.png`](reports/figures/families3d_qwen3.5-2b.png). [Interactive 3-D, with a choice of axes](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-families).

**The pre-specified decision rule for "angles have a circular component beyond PC1–2"** requires all four conditions at the preregistered layer. Score: the best closed-cycle score over the 10 planes of PC1–5. p: a permutation p of that maximum.

{{table:planes_decision:all}}

For days and months, every model:

{{table:planes:all}}

- **Days:** close in the top-2 plane in three of five models.
- **Months:** close in a lower plane (PC2–PC3, PC4–PC5) in three of five.
- **Twin:** one twin (Qwen2.5-1.5B) also shows a closed months loop. Word form alone can occasionally produce one, so these p-values (unadjusted, one per cell) are descriptive.
- **Power:** with the closure rule the test is conservative ([amendment 2 of the addendum](reports/prereg_addendum_3d.md)), so it can miss weak cycles.

![ordered chains]({{fig:chains_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the class-inclusion chains in the PC plane, trained (top) and twin (bottom), with the Robinson score below each panel.
- **What to notice:** the ring and space chains run as ordered paths and stay ordered after word frequency and token count are removed. In the twin they collapse to a tangle.
- **Caveat:** two twins also order the ring chain beyond frequency, so word form ("… domain") carries part of that order. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-families).

#### Axioms as directions

![axiom lattice facets]({{fig:lattice_axes_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** left, the ideal geometry, where each axiom is one fixed step. Each other panel is the same unsupervised PCA plane, highlighting the pairs that differ only in one axiom.
- **What to notice:** in the trained model the highlighted arrows point roughly the same way; in the twin they point everywhere.
- **Caveat:** a 2-D picture can hide or exaggerate parallelism; the next figure shows the full-dimensional evidence. [Interactive, with an analogy playground](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-lattice).

![axiom lattice in 3-D]({{fig:lattice3d_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the same facets in the structures' top-3 principal components, with true proportions and one fixed camera for every model. Blue 3-D arrows are the pairs that differ only in that axiom.
- **What to notice:** the third axis keeps the trained model's arrows roughly parallel, while the twin's still point every way.
- **Caveat:** a 3-D view can still hide or exaggerate parallelism; the cosine matrix below is the evidence. On the site you can rotate it, choose any 3 of the top-5 PCs, and see the analogy query b − a + c placed exactly. [Interactive 3-D](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-lattice).

![offset cosine matrices]({{fig:lattice_cosines_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the cosine between every pair of single-axiom difference vectors, grouped by axiom.
- **What to notice:** bright red diagonal blocks mean "adding this axiom" is a consistent direction. They are clear for associativity and commutativity, and weaker for identity and divisibility. The dot plot on the right shows that the offsets survive removing the token-count direction.
- **Caveat:** hatched cells are cross-axiom pairs that share a structure; their cosine is about ±0.5 even for random vectors, so they carry no evidence. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-cosines).

![group objects]({{fig:group_objects}})

- **What you see:** left, how parallel the three parallelograms are (for example, Lie group − topological group vs smooth manifold − topological space) in every model and twin. Right, where "group" and "smooth manifold" rank among the neighbours of "Lie group".
- **What to notice:** every trained model clears the null (Qwen3.5-2B: {{num:mvp.structures.qwen3.5-2b.group_objects.parallelograms.cos:.2f}}). Trained models place "Lie group" near both parents. The twins put "group" nearest, and except for Gemma's twin place "smooth manifold" far away.
- **Caveat:** exploratory, and the twins' closeness to "group" is purely lexical (shared token). [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-groups).

![partial-operation lattice]({{fig:partial_operation}})

- **What you see:** a negative result. Offset consistency for the partial-operation lattice (semigroupoid, small category, groupoid vs semigroup, monoid, group) in all models and twins, against the random-pair null.
- **What to notice:** no axis clears the null in Qwen3.5-2B ("total" operation: {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.audit2.partial_operation.offsets.total.consistency:.2f}}, null 95th percentile {{num:mvp.lattice.qwen3.5-2b.audit2.partial_operation.offsets.total.null95:.2f}}).
- **Caveat:** with 6 items and 2–3 pairs per axis, this test has little power; "no evidence" is not evidence of absence. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-partial).

#### Concrete ↔ abstract

![abstraction axis]({{fig:abstraction_qwen3.5-2b}})

- **What you see:** the {{num:mvp.map_fields.qwen3.5-2b.math_primary.n}} primary concepts on their first two principal components (after frequency and token count are removed), coloured by judge abstraction (left) and pure/applied (middle). Right: judge ratings vs the Mathlib import depth of each concept's definition.
- **What to notice:** PC1 runs from concrete to abstract (ρ = {{num:mvp.axes.qwen3.5-2b.pcs.0.rho_abstraction:.2f}}, twin {{num:mvp.axes.qwen3.5-2b__random.pcs.0.rho_abstraction:.2f}}), and PC2 from pure to applied. The judges' ratings rise with Mathlib depth.
- **Caveat:** ratings come from LLM judges, and only {{num:mvp.mathlib.n_matched}} concepts could be matched to Mathlib. [Interactive](https://burnycoder.github.io/geometry-of-representations-of-mathematics-in-llms/#fig-abstraction).
